question: In \(\triangle ADE,\) \(\angle ADE=140^\circ,\) points \(B\) and \(C\) lie on sides \(AD\) and \(AE,\) respectively, and points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) \(E\) are distinct. If lengths \(AB,\) \(BC,\) \(CD,\) and \(DE\) are all equal, then the measure of \(\angle EAD\) is
solution:
The equal lengths create three isosceles triangles, \(ABC\), \(BCD\), and \(CDE\), whose base angles link the desired angle to \(140^\circ\).

Let \(\theta=\angle EAD\). Triangle \(ADE\) gives
\[
\angle AED=40^\circ-\theta,
\qquad 0<\theta<40^\circ.
\]
Because all five points are distinct, \(B\) lies strictly between \(A\) and \(D\), and \(C\) lies strictly between \(A\) and \(E\).

Since \(AB=BC\), the base angles of triangle \(ABC\) satisfy
\[
\angle BAC=\angle ACB=\theta.
\]
Thus \(\angle ABC=180^\circ-2\theta\). Rays \(BA\) and \(BD\) are opposite, so \(\angle CBD=2\theta\). Now \(BC=CD\), so triangle \(BCD\) has equal base angles at \(B\) and \(D\). Hence
\[
\angle CDA=\angle CDB=2\theta.
\]
Since \(DC\) lies inside \(\angle ADE\), we obtain \(\angle CDE=140^\circ-2\theta\).

Finally, \(CD=DE\), so the base angles of triangle \(CDE\) at \(C\) and \(E\) are equal. Its angle at \(E\) is \(\angle CED=\angle AED=40^\circ-\theta\). The angle sum in triangle \(CDE\) therefore gives
\[
(140^\circ-2\theta)+2(40^\circ-\theta)=180^\circ.
\]
Thus \(4\theta=40^\circ\), so \(\theta=10^\circ\), which lies in the required range. Therefore \(\boxed{\angle EAD=10^\circ}\), choice E.
